message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most effective exercises you can do to target all the major muscle groups in your legs—quads, hamstrings, glutes, calves, and even the inner/outer thighs. I’ll include a few variations so you can mix things up and keep your routine fresh.

| Exercise | Primary Muscles Worked | Key Tips / Variations |
|----------|------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Squat** (body‑weight, goblet, barbell back/ front) | Quads, glutes, hamstrings, core | Keep your chest up, knees tracking over toes, and drive through the heels. Add a pause at the bottom for time‑under‑tension. |
| **Lunge** (forward, reverse, walking, stationary) | Quads, glutes, hamstrings, calves | Step far enough that the front knee stays above the ankle. For more challenge, hold dumbbells or use a weighted vest. |
| **Deadlift** (conventional, sumo, Romanian) | Hamstrings, glutes, lower back, traps | Maintain a neutral spine, hinge at the hips, and keep the bar close to your shins. Romanian deadlifts are great for isolating the hamstrings. |
| **Leg Press** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Adjust foot placement to emphasize different parts of the quads; higher foot placement targets the glutes more. |
| **Calf Raise** (standing, seated, single‑leg) | Calves (gastrocnemius & soleus) | Perform slow eccentric (lowering) phases for better growth. Use a full range of motion—full stretch at the top, full contraction at the bottom. |
| **Bulgarian Split Squat** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Elevate the rear foot on a bench or box. Keep torso upright and push through the front heel. |
| **Step‑Up** (onto a bench or box) | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Use a high box for a deeper hip flexion. Add dumbbells for extra resistance. |
| **Hip Thrust / Glute Bridge** | Glutes, hamstrings, core | Drive through the heels, squeeze at the top, and pause for 1–2 seconds before lowering. |
| **Hamstring Curl** (lying or seated machine) | Hamstrings | Focus on controlled movement; avoid using momentum. |
| **Side Lunge / Curtsy Lunge** | Inner/outer thighs, glutes | Keep the knee tracking over the toes and maintain a slight bend in the back knee. |

### How to Structure a Leg‑Day Routine

1. **Warm‑up** – 5–10 min of light cardio (bike, treadmill, or jump rope) + dynamic stretches (leg swings, hip circles).  
2. **Compound Movements** – Start with the big lifts (squat, deadlift, leg press) while you’re freshest.  
3. **Isolation / Accessory Work** – Follow with lunges, step‑ups, hip thrusts, and calf raises.  
4. **Cool‑down** – Light static stretching focusing on quads, hamstrings, calves, and glutes.  

### Sample 3‑Day Split

| Day | Focus | Example Sets/Reps |
|-----|-------|-------------------|
| **Leg Day 1** | Strength | Back squat 4×6, Romanian deadlift 3×8, Leg press 3×10 |
| **Leg Day 2** | Hypertrophy | Bulgarian split squat 3×12, Hip thrust 3×15, Calf raise 4×20 |
| **Leg Day 3** | Endurance / Conditioning | Walking lunge 3×20, Step‑up 3×15, Seated hamstring curl 3×15 |

Feel free to adjust the volume (sets/reps) based on your training level and goals. If you’re new, start with lighter weights and focus on form; as you progress, increase load or add supersets for intensity. Happy training!
